# Ambiguity audit: "17/190 canonical SMILES map to multiple extractant_name"

*Run 2026-08-19. Generated by `runs/gen7_architecture/ambiguity_audit.py`; every number below is reproduced by that script and mirrored in `ambiguity_audit.json`.*

## Verdict

**World C ("the ambiguity is a missing-variable ceiling") is rejected on the data.** The warning is not a chemistry signal. Sixteen of the seventeen ambiguous SMILES are *synonym duplicates* — an acronym and its IUPAC name, or two paper-local labels for one molecule. The seventeenth is a **wrong-structure batch**: the TODGA SMILES string is pasted onto 19 chemically distinct ligands.

Once you condition on everything the level model can actually see (metal + the full 64-column `cond__` vector), only **73 rows in 22 cells** in the whole dataset carry two names under one SMILES — and **all of them are the TODGA batch** (removing TODGA leaves zero rows). On those rows `extractant_name` has a permutation-adjusted eta^2 of **-0.082** (p = 0.53): it explains *nothing* beyond a random partition of the same granularity.

And the cleanest single number: once the three identified defects (the TODGA batch, the DMDPhPDA decimal corruption, the C5BTBP diluent split) are removed, rows that share a SMILES but differ in name agree **better** than genuine same-name replicates — RMS |Δlog_D| 0.694 (n=37) against a replicate floor of 1.325 (n=4226). The remaining aliases are not carrying hidden chemistry; they are carrying nothing.

The audit did find a genuine missing variable, but it is somewhere else: the **aqueous-phase complexant** (DTPA, TEDGA, DOODA(C2), NaNO3, amic acid, malonamide, HEDTA, BTP-4Me, CDTA) on **557 rows (9.3 %)**, recorded only inside the free-text `comments_description` column. It has no `cond__` feature and the structured `Holdback_Agent_Name` column is NULL on all 48138 upstream rows.

## (b) Is the name split explained by a recoverable upstream variable?

**No — and the question is the wrong one for 16 of the 17.** The name difference is not a chemical difference; the two names denote one molecule. The specific fields asked about:

| upstream field | verdict across the 17 groups |
|---|---|
| `Holdback_Agent_Name` | **NULL on all 48138 upstream rows** — the column exists and was never filled. It separates nothing, anywhere. |
| `Phase_Modifier_Name` | Non-null on 239 of 3011 ambiguous rows. Never a function of the name in any of the 17 groups. |
| `Solvent_Name` | Determines the name in 11/17 groups — but only because each synonym came from a different publication that used a different diluent. Correlational, not causal: the diluent does not *make* the ligand have two names. |
| `DOI` / `entry_author` | Determines the name in most groups (the synonym is a curator/publication artefact). This is the real generator of the ambiguity. |
| `ini_comp`, `comments_description` | Recover the name in 17/17 — but they literally contain the extractant name as a substring. Excluded as leaky. |

### The one group where the name *is* the chemistry: TODGA

`CCCCCCCCN(CCCCCCCC)C(=O)COCC(=O)N(CCCCCCCC)CCCCCCCC` carries **1714 rows under 21 names**. 111 of them, spread over 19 distinct ligands, are not TODGA at all:

`PHEN-6OH`, `PyTri-Tetraol`, `PHEN-dialcohol`, `TWE-40`, `TWE-26`, `CITAM`, `SO3-Ph-BTP`, `SO3-Ph-BTBP`, `TWE-41`, `TWE-42`, `(PhSO3Na)2-BTBP`, `(PhSO3Na)2-BTPhen`, `PyTri-diol`, `TWE-39`, `TWE-31`, `TWE-32`, `TWE-37`, `TWE-38`, `PPA`

(The 21st name, `TODGA,DHOA`, is a legitimate composite-solvent label — its upstream SMILES is `<TODGA>,-` — and accounts for the other 18 non-TODGA rows.)

Upstream the damage is wider: **742 rows across 21 distinct `Extractant_Name` values** carry the exact TODGA SMILES string. Every affected dataset row comes from a single curator (Baosen Zhang) and a single ingest batch. These are real, chemically distinct ligands — sulfonated BTP/BTBP complexants, phenanthroline diols, PyTri polyols, the TWE-2x/3x/4x screening series — whose `Extractant_SMILES` field was filled with TODGA.

Recoverability: `Holdback_Agent_Name` = ['<NA>'], `Phase_Modifier_Name` = ['<NA>']. Nothing structured recovers the real molecule. `ini_comp` names the true ligand on 100 % of these rows but carries no structure. **The correct SMILES is not in the bundle** — this is a fix that has to happen upstream.

**Scope check.** The TWE screening series is *not* systematically broken: of 34 TWE codes upstream, 25 distinct SMILES are recorded and only 10 of them collapse onto TODGA (`TWE-18`, `TWE-26`, `TWE-31`, `TWE-32`, `TWE-37`, `TWE-38`, `TWE-39`, `TWE-40`, `TWE-41`, `TWE-42`). The rest carry chemically sensible, distinct structures — thiophosphinates, phosphonates, furandiamides, NTA-amides. That localises the defect to one copy-paste inside one batch, and it is why the other alias pairs (TWE-11/NTAamide(C8), TWE-14/Me2-TODGA, TWE-15/NEA16, TWE-17/18b, TWE-21/10a, TWE-22/NEA15) are safe to read as synonyms rather than as further corruption.

### A second defect the audit turned up: a decimal-corrupted double entry

`CN(C(=O)c1cccc(C(=O)N(C)c2ccccc2)n1)c1ccccc1` = DMDPhPDA, 70 matched (metal, HNO3) cells, entered **twice** from the *same* paper (DOI `10.1081/SEI-120030392`, Shimada et al. 2003) by two curators (Baosen Zhang, Thomas Summers), under an acronym and its IUPAC name.

The pairwise difference in log_D is **an exact integer in every single cell** (`delta_logD_is_an_exact_integer_in_every_cell = True`):

| Δ log_D | cells | D ratio |
|---|---|---|
| 0.0 | 11 | 10^0 |
| 1.0 | 17 | 10^1 |
| 2.0 | 14 | 10^2 |
| 3.0 | 14 | 10^3 |
| 4.0 | 14 | 10^4 |

One copy kept only the mantissa of the paper's Table 1 and dropped the ×10^−n exponent. **70 dataset rows carry log_D wrong by 1–4 orders of magnitude.** This is label corruption, not a missing variable.

It is also a *feature* corruption: the two entries wrote the diluent as `CH3Cl` and `Chloroform`, which map to two different dummies. `cond__diluent__ch3cl` has 84 rows in the whole dataset, 70 of them (83 %) this one corruption. Any tree that splits on `cond__diluent__ch3cl` is learning "this value is 10^n too high", dressed up as a chemistry effect.

### And one group where the split genuinely is a recoverable variable

C5BTBP vs its IUPAC name shows a 2.31 log-unit offset at cell-P matched conditions — but the two names sit in different diluents (IUPAC name: cyclohexanone; C5BTBP: 1-decanol, 1-heptanol, 1-hexanol, 1-nonanol, …), different publications and different temperatures. Both diluents already have `cond__diluent__*` features (cyclohexanone: True, kerosene 0.7/1-octanol 0.3: True). The offset is fully model-visible; the cell-P key was simply too coarse. This is why the whole analysis is repeated below on the model-visible cell.

## (c) Variance decomposition

For each cell definition: residual after removing the (SMILES × cell) mean, then how much of that residual `extractant_name` explains. Because names are near-singleton inside a cell, the raw eta^2 is inflated by degrees of freedom; every eta^2 below is reported **raw, against a 400-draw permutation null (names shuffled within cell), and adjusted** as `(obs − null)/(1 − null)`.

### Cell P — metal + ox + acid + [acid] + [extractant]

| subset | rows | cells | RMS \|Δlog_D\| between names | RMS \|Δlog_D\| within a name | eta^2 raw | eta^2 null | **eta^2 adj** | perm p | residual sd |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| all 17 ambiguous SMILES | 374 | 134 | 1.939 (n=544) | 1.566 (n=374) | 0.838 | 0.801 | **0.183** | 0.080 | 1.374 |
| excl. the TODGA batch | 231 | 113 | 2.067 (n=120) | 0.378 (n=6) | 0.999 | 0.988 | **0.890** | 0.188 | 1.466 |
| excl. TODGA + DMDPhPDA | 91 | 43 | 1.340 (n=50) | 0.378 (n=6) | 0.992 | 0.934 | **0.880** | 0.217 | 0.937 |
| excl. TODGA + DMDPhPDA + C5BTBP (the 3 known defects) | 65 | 30 | 0.694 (n=37) | 0.378 (n=6) | 0.946 | 0.521 | **0.888** | 0.205 | 0.420 |
| *replicate floor* (cells with ≥2 rows, **one** name) | 1893 | 523 | — | 1.325 (n=4226) | — | — | — | — | 0.922 |

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| all 17 ambiguous SMILES | 73 | 22 | 1.849 (n=99) | 1.517 (n=26) | 0.815 | 0.829 | **-0.082** | 0.527 | 1.375 |

### How much of the name effect do the recoverable upstream fields explain?

| cell | key | eta^2 raw | eta^2 null | eta^2 adj | perm p |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P | extractant_name | 0.838 | 0.801 | 0.183 | 0.080 |
| P | upstream condition fields (14, incl. Solvent/Phase_Modifier/Holdback) | 0.696 | 0.695 | 0.004 | 0.400 |
| P | + DOI / entry_author / source file | 0.699 | 0.710 | -0.037 | 0.715 |
| M | extractant_name | 0.815 | 0.829 | -0.082 | 0.527 |
| M | upstream condition fields (14, incl. Solvent/Phase_Modifier/Holdback) | 0.000 | 0.000 | 0.000 | 1.000 |
| M | + DOI / entry_author / source file | 0.015 | 0.039 | -0.024 | 0.815 |

With the three identified defects removed, only 65 rows in 30 cells remain contested on cell P, and the between-name RMS |Δlog_D| falls to 0.694 against a replicate floor of 1.325. The permutation-adjusted eta^2 in the trimmed subsets is high but uninterpretable: there are only 6 within-name replicate pairs left to define the null, so the name partition is essentially saturated. Treat those rows as effect sizes, not as variance shares.

**Reading.** On cell P the name looks like it explains 84 % of the within-cell residual, but a random partition of the same granularity explains 80 %; the adjusted figure is 0.18 at p = 0.08. The upstream condition fields explain 0.004 adjusted (p = 0.40) — i.e. **nothing**. On the model-visible cell M the adjusted eta^2 for the name is negative and p = 0.52.

**The comparison that settles it.** At model-visible matched conditions, replicate rows that share one name already disagree by RMS |Δlog_D| = 1.170 (32 % of pairs differ by more than a full log unit). Rows that differ in name disagree by RMS 1.849. The ambiguity adds essentially nothing on top of a replicate floor that is already enormous.

## The missing variable that *is* real: the aqueous complexant

Chasing the replicate floor above led to it. `comments_description` carries a semi-structured block; parsing `Complexant_Name:` out of it yields:

| complexant | rows |
|---|---|
| *(none)* | 5435 |
| DTPA | 165 |
| TEDGA | 88 |
| DOODA(C2) | 88 |
| NaNO3 | 70 |
| Amicacid | 69 |
| malonamide | 56 |
| HEDTA | 10 |
| BTP-4Me | 10 |
| CDTA | 1 |

**557 rows (9.3 %) carry an aqueous-phase complexant that the model cannot see.** DTPA, HEDTA, CDTA and TEDGA are precisely the holdback agents that suppress trivalent-actinide/lanthanide distribution by orders of magnitude.

- structured `Holdback_Agent_Name` non-null anywhere upstream: **0**
- dataset features matching complexant/holdback/DTPA/TEDGA/DOODA: **none**

Inside replicated (SMILES × metal × full `cond__` vector) cells:

| statistic | value |
|---|---|
| replicated cells / rows | 313 / 1003 |
| residual sd inside those cells | 0.776 |
| oracle MAE floor on those cells | 0.402 |
| residual sd where the complexant **varies** | 0.944 (51 cells) |
| residual sd where the complexant is **constant** | 0.634 |
| RMS \|Δlog_D\| between differing complexants | 1.484 (n=833) |
| RMS \|Δlog_D\| within the same complexant | 0.939 (n=961) |
| **eta^2 of complexant within model cell** | raw 0.454, null 0.221, **adjusted 0.299**, p = 0.000 |
| control: DOI within model cell | raw 0.003, adjusted -0.000, p = 1.00 |

Mean cell-centred log_D by complexant (matched conditions, so this is the complexant's own effect):

| complexant | n | mean cell-centred log_D |
|---|---|---|
| TEDGA | 86 | -0.567 |
| DOODA(C2) | 86 | -0.257 |
| BTP-4Me | 10 | -0.006 |
| DTPA | 108 | -0.000 |
| HEDTA | 10 | +0.000 |
| NaNO3 | 28 | +0.000 |
| *(none)* | 592 | +0.082 |
| Amicacid | 27 | +0.161 |
| malonamide | 56 | +0.325 |

TEDGA depresses log_D by 0.57 and malonamide raises it by 0.33 relative to the same cell — both invisible to the current feature set. **This** is the missing-variable ceiling, and unlike the name ambiguity it is recoverable: the field is sitting in the comments string.

## Live pipeline impact

`extractant = canonical_smiles (levels.py:409); the level cell is (extractant, condition_id, metal_symbol) with condition_id built from cond__* only`.

- `src/lanthanide_separation/pairs.py::apply_default_quarantine` **already knows about the TODGA defect** (reason `todga_structure_assigned_to_different_extractant`).
- **`scripts/run_gen5_levels.py`, `scripts/gen6_phase0.py` and the gen7 harness never call it.** They read `dataset.parquet` straight into `levels.build_level_dataset`.
- Result: **129 rows caught by that predicate (`canonical_smiles == TODGA and extractant_name != 'TODGA'` — the 111 wrong-structure rows plus the 18 legitimate `TODGA,DHOA` rows) enter 69 level cells attributed to TODGA** — 4.6 % of TODGA's 1488 level cells are another molecule's data. They do *not* get averaged into real TODGA cells (0 mixed cells) because their diluents differ — they arrive as extra, wrong cells instead.
- DMDPhPDA contributes 140 level cells and the two curator entries **do not merge** (0 merged cells): Solvent_Name `CH3Cl` vs `Chloroform` map to two different `cond__diluent__` dummies, so the level cohort holds the same molecule twice with log_D differing by up to 4 orders of magnitude, presented to the model as a diluent contrast.

---

## Actions

1. **Call `apply_default_quarantine` (or an equivalent filter) in the level pipeline.** 129 rows, 69 level cells, one line of code. Currently only the pair pipeline is protected.
2. **Quarantine the 70 mantissa-only DMDPhPDA rows** — `extractant_name == "2-N-6-N-dimethyl-2-N-6-N-diphenylpyridine-2-6-dicarboxamide"`, all in `Am_SAFE`, exp_id 16085–16154 (contiguous), curator Baosen Zhang, `Solvent_Name = "CH3Cl"` — and drop or merge `cond__diluent__ch3cl`, which is 83 % this corruption.
3. **Collapse the 16 synonym groups on `canonical_smiles`.** gen6 already does this (`extractant = canonical_smiles`); anything that groups or splits on `extractant_name` would leak a molecule across a held-out-ligand boundary. No current harness does — worth a regression test.
4. **Parse `Complexant_Name` / `Complexant_Concentration_M` out of `comments_description` into a `cond__` block.** 557 rows, adjusted eta^2 0.30 of the residual inside perfectly matched model-visible cells, p < 0.003 (0 of 400 permutations reached the observed value). This is the first concretely recoverable variable the audit found.
5. Do **not** treat the ambiguity warning as evidence for a capacity/ceiling argument. It is a curation defect of ~200 rows plus 16 harmless aliases.
